summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science background: asymptotic analysis, discrete mathematics (binary numbers, modular arithmetic, primes, XOR, subsets), introductory linear algebra (matrices, invertibility, vector subspaces, dimension), and basic complex numbers and polynomials. They know basic Turing machines with tapes, and have seen the standard FFT idea at most as an algorithm, not the Nussbaumer, Bluestein or Harvey-van der Hoeven machinery. They have not studied algebraic number theory, advanced algebra such as Bruhat factorization, or numerical error analysis in depth.

known.name: Binary representation of integers
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a string of bits with place values powers of two, padded with leading zeros to a fixed length.

known.name: Logarithms and ceiling/floor
known.gloss: lg n is the base-2 logarithm, and ceiling and floor round a real number up or down to an integer.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers where numbers differing by a multiple of m are identified, with addition and multiplication well defined on residues.

known.name: Prime numbers and coprimality
known.gloss: A prime has no divisors besides 1 and itself, and integers are coprime when their greatest common divisor is 1.

known.name: Bitwise XOR
known.gloss: The bit operation giving 1 exactly when its two inputs differ, equal to addition modulo 2, and self-inverse.

known.name: Matrices and linear maps
known.gloss: Linear maps between vector spaces are represented by matrices, composed by matrix multiplication, invertible when an inverse exists, and triangular when entries above or below the diagonal vanish.

known.name: Vector subspaces and dimension
known.gloss: A subspace is a set of vectors closed under addition and scaling, with dimension equal to the size of any basis.

known.name: Cartesian product and index sets
known.gloss: The set of tuples with each coordinate from its own set, used to index multidimensional arrays.

known.name: Permutations
known.gloss: A permutation is a bijective rearrangement of a finite set of positions.

known.name: Fixed-point and rounding
known.gloss: Real numbers are stored as integers scaled by a power of two, and rounding or truncation discards low-order digits, introducing a bounded error.

known.name: Absolute value, modulus and sup norm
known.gloss: Size measures for numbers and vectors, with the sup norm the largest absolute entry, obeying the triangle inequality.

known.name: Schoolbook multiplication and carries
known.gloss: The grade-school method of multiplying numbers digit by digit and propagating carries, taking quadratic time.

known.name: Divide and conquer recursion
known.gloss: Solving a problem by recursive calls on smaller instances and combining results, with running time analysed by a recurrence.

known.name: Induction and proof by contradiction
known.gloss: Standard proof techniques used throughout discrete mathematics.

known.name: Linear-time scanning of tape data
known.gloss: A Turing machine head can read, copy or transform an n-cell tape contents in time proportional to n by sweeping across it.

known.name: Euclidean division and floor division
known.gloss: Every integer a and positive m give a unique quotient q and remainder r with a = qm + r and 0 <= r < m.

known.name: Geometric series and exponent rules
known.gloss: Sums of the form 1 + r + r^2 + ... have closed forms, and powers obey the usual exponent laws.
